title: A New Research Agenda for AI Constitutionalism
gist: A newly formed Working Group on AI Constitutionalism argues that the value documents frontier labs use to steer their models — Claude's Constitution, OpenAI's Model Spec, Google DeepMind's Gemini policy guidelines — are drafted by a handful of unrepresentative lab employees with no third-party oversight, and lays out a four-strand research agenda (values, process/authority, technical, enforcement) to push toward democratic legitimacy. It flags that alignment training is actually working (citing very low reported misalignment in Anthropic's latest models), which raises rather than lowers the stakes of who writes the rules and how value conflicts get adjudicated.

themes.theme: AI constitutions as the new governance surface

insights.claim: The public-facing value documents frontier labs publish — Anthropic's Claude's Constitution, OpenAI's Model Spec, Google DeepMind's Gemini policy guidelines — are emerging as the de facto governance layer for AI, because they specify the principles, rules, and cases that determine model behavior at global scale.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Constitution and model-spec documents are cheap, public, and updated frequently — read them as leading indicators of product policy, refusal surface, and regulatory exposure before regulation arrives.
insights.quote: AI constitutions—the high-level, public-facing documents that specify the principles, rules, and cases intended to align the model with the lab’s mission—offer a potential vehicle for contestation.
insights.locator: Frontier artificial intelligence (AI) systems have

insights.claim: Three properties make AI constitutions unusually useful governance instruments: they are legible to laypeople as well as experts, influential because they shape how billions of people interact with AI, and amendable so they can be updated as stakeholder preferences change.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A reusable three-test filter (legible, influential, amendable) for judging whether any proposed AI-governance artifact will actually bind behavior.
insights.locator: At least three characteristics of AI constitutions

insights.claim: Labs have deliberately avoided equating their constitutions to the U.S. Constitution, because these documents are drafted behind closed doors and enforced with no third-party oversight — meaning the word 'constitution' claims an authority the labs do not actually hold.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The legitimacy gap is the wedge a future regulator or plaintiff will use; expect pressure for external audit of constitution drafting and enforcement.
insights.quote: The word “constitution,” whether intended or not by the labs, presumes an authority that AI developers do not clearly hold and that the public has not granted.
insights.locator: A Call for a More Perfect Process

insights.claim: Even where the drafting and enforcement of AI constitutions remain opaque, the documents themselves are published, which already permits a form of public scrutiny that no other part of the training stack allows.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The published constitution is the only externally auditable artifact in frontier model development — the natural anchor point for any disclosure regime.
insights.locator: Though the drafting and enforcement of AI constitutions

themes.theme: What the labs actually commit to

insights.claim: Anthropic instructs Claude to weigh users' long-term flourishing rather than only their immediate stated request — for example noticing user stress behind a coding request — while explicitly avoiding paternalism or dishonesty.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Wellbeing-weighted helpfulness is a product differentiator and a liability posture; it predicts where Claude will push back versus comply in consumer and enterprise settings.
insights.quote: we want Claude’s helpfulness to flow from deep and genuine care for users’ overall flourishing, without being paternalistic or dishonest.
insights.locator: Claude should pay attention to user wellbeing

insights.claim: OpenAI's Model Spec contains 'red-line principles' that categorically foreclose facilitating critical and high-severity harms including violence, cyber/biological/nuclear weapons creation, terrorism, child abuse, persecution, and mass surveillance.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: These hard red lines define the outer boundary of addressable defense, biosecurity, and surveillance markets for OpenAI models — a structural constraint on where its models can be sold.
insights.quote: facilitat[ing] critical and high severity harms, such as acts of violence, creation of cyber, biological or nuclear weapons, terrorism, child abuse, persecution or mass surveillance.
insights.locator: AI constitutions may also include more concrete instructions

insights.claim: Google DeepMind takes a more fragmented disclosure approach than its rivals, with 'policy guidelines' as the nearest analog to a Model Spec or constitution and a stated goal of being maximally helpful while avoiding real-world harm or offense.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Google is the transparency laggard among the big three on model values — a differentiated exposure if disclosure norms harden into requirements.
insights.quote: Our goal for the Gemini app is to be maximally helpful to users, while avoiding outputs that could cause real-world harm or offense.
insights.locator: Google DeepMind takes a more fragmented approach

insights.claim: All three major labs concede their models do not reliably adhere to their own stated values: OpenAI says models presently fall short, Anthropic commits to disclosing divergence in system cards released with each model, and Google calls the alignment technically tricky.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Self-admitted non-adherence is documented in public filings — a ready-made evidentiary base for enforcement actions or litigation over model behavior.
insights.quote: Model adherence to the constitution is also a work in progress.
insights.locator: We the Labs: The Pitfalls of Propriety AI Constitutionalism

themes.theme: Alignment training is working — which raises the stakes

insights.claim: Anthropic's most recent models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, show very low rates of reported misalignment, and OpenAI reports general progress on key alignment measures for its most recent model — evidence that constitution-style behavioral training is effective.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: If value documents reliably transmit to model behavior, whoever controls the document controls the behavior of systems used by billions — making the drafting process, not the technique, the contested asset.
insights.quote: Anthropic’s most recent models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, have very low rates of reported misalignment, for example.
insights.locator: Technical limitations notwithstanding

insights.claim: Models are more aligned when trained on data in which the model itself acts in accordance with the developer's values and goals, making curated behavioral demonstration data a direct input to alignment quality.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Behavioral training corpora are a compounding proprietary asset — labs with better value-consistent data get better-aligned models, a moat that isn't compute.
insights.quote: Related research has shown that models tend to be more aligned when exposed to data in which the model acts in accordance with the developer’s values and goals.
insights.locator: Technical limitations notwithstanding

insights.claim: There is a genuine tension between alignment transparency and security: granular disclosure of how behavioral training works could hand bad actors a roadmap for subverting that training, which gives labs a defensible reason to keep parts of the process secret.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Expect labs to use this security argument to resist granular disclosure mandates — the fight will be over what tier of transparency is safe, not whether to disclose.
insights.quote: Granular transparency about behavioral training could hand bad actors a roadmap for subverting that very training.
insights.locator: Yet, there may be important reasons

insights.claim: The decisive governance question is not which values a constitution enumerates but how values are operationalized in context and how conflicts among them are adjudicated, since a document that leaves every hard case to undisclosed ad hoc resolution has settled nothing.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Judge lab governance claims by their conflict-resolution machinery, not their value lists — the absence of a stated adjudication process is the real red flag.
insights.quote: An AI constitution that enumerates good values while leaving every hard case to undisclosed, ad hoc resolution procedures has settled little.
insights.locator: Progress on adherence, however, raises the stakes

insights.claim: Embedded model values silently shape user behavior in high-stakes domains — relationship guidance, financial advice, medical advice, strategic decisionmaking — often without users realizing a foundation model is operating behind the tool they are using.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Downstream apps inherit upstream model values invisibly — a hidden concentration risk for any sector where a handful of foundation models sit under thousands of products.
insights.quote: by virtue of these foundational models often operating behind the scenes of other tools, users may have no clue that those values are silently, yet significantly shaping the AI’s work product
insights.locator: Why Model Values Matter

insights.claim: Agentic tools may have orders of magnitude more impact than chatbots because users spin up agents that act autonomously on their behalf in legally and morally significant activities, running for days with varying degrees of oversight.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Agent autonomy converts model-value questions into legal-liability questions; watch for the first litigation attributing an agent's autonomous act to the model developer's constitution.
insights.quote: agentic tools may have orders of magnitude more impact as they are deployed in sensitive contexts, with varying degrees of oversight
insights.locator: The possibility of models having even more consequential

insights.claim: Users have already taken irreversible and harmful actions at the direction of AI models, meaning the harm scenario the agenda addresses is realized rather than speculative.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Realized harm is the precondition for tort exposure and for legislative urgency — the 'no demonstrated harm' defense is already unavailable.
insights.quote: Some users have already taken irreversible and harmful actions at the direction of AI models.
insights.locator: Why Model Values Matter

insights.claim: As AI systems become more capable and autonomous, humans will be less involved in scrutinizing discrete outputs, so human-in-the-loop review will stop functioning as the primary oversight mechanism and must be replaced by alternative means of contestation.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Compliance products built on per-output human review have a shrinking addressable window; document-level and process-level oversight is the growth area.
insights.quote: If humans are not in the “loop”—actively scrutinizing discrete AI outputs—as frequently, alternative means of oversight must be developed.
insights.locator: Frontier artificial intelligence (AI) systems have

themes.theme: The legitimacy deficit and the pluralism counter-frame

insights.claim: AI constitutions are currently drafted informally inside labs by a select few employees whose views and experiences are unrepresentative of the United States and even more unrepresentative of the labs' growing global user bases.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The representativeness gap between drafters and users is the most likely trigger for foreign regulatory intervention in non-U.S. markets.
insights.locator: AI labs currently develop constitutions in an informal fashion

insights.claim: A growing research line argues the search for one correct value set is the wrong frame entirely — for many contested questions the goal should be models that faithfully represent a range of reasonable positions and can be transparently steered toward different value frames by context and user.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Steerable, frame-disclosing models are a plausible product direction that sidesteps the 'whose values' fight — a differentiator for any lab that ships it first.
insights.quote: the goal should instead be systems that can faithfully represent a range of reasonable positions and be steered, transparently, toward different value frames depending on context and user
insights.locator: But this agenda also addresses the counter-hypothetical

insights.claim: Under the pluralism frame, the public's role shifts from picking values to setting the bounds within which pluralism is permitted, governing the procedures that resolve value conflicts, and holding developers accountable for disclosing and adhering to whichever frame they operate under.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: This reframes future regulation as disclosure-plus-adherence auditing rather than value mandates — a far lighter and more likely legislative template.
insights.locator: It may also be that the public’s role

insights.claim: AI constitutionalism has a dual ambition: restraining, by subjecting developer discretion to contestable public-facing limits, and affirmative, by building models that actively strengthen the preconditions of liberal democracy — pluralism, deliberation, and accountable power.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The affirmative ambition is the more radical ask — it implies models should be evaluated on democratic externalities, a metric no lab currently reports.
insights.quote: Its affirmative ambition is to build models that actively strengthen the preconditions of liberal democracy: pluralism, deliberation, and accountable power.
insights.locator: Answers to these questions are the basis

insights.claim: Making constitutions the vehicle of governance creates its own risk: because they effectively shape model values, they become a high-value target for capture by biased actors or bending toward political interests.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Political capture of a model constitution would be a low-visibility, high-leverage influence vector — worth monitoring as an information-integrity risk.
insights.quote: their efficacy in shaping model values also raises significant risks of constitutions being captured by biased actors or bent toward political interests
insights.locator: So while constitutions are a potential vehicle

insights.claim: The social media era is the explicit cautionary analogy: had its harms been mitigated through regular, meaningful public engagement via formal processes, its benefits might also have been further developed and spread — implying participatory governance is upside-generating, not just harm-reducing.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Framing oversight as value-creating rather than value-taxing is the argument likely to win over industry — watch which labs adopt it.
insights.quote: If social media’s many ills had been mitigated with more regular and meaningful public engagement via formal processes, its benefits may have also been further developed and spread.
insights.locator: Increased scholarly attention to AI Constitutionalism

themes.theme: The research agenda and its institutional backing

insights.claim: A Working Group on AI Constitutionalism spanning Yale, Oxford, Stanford, JHU, UT Austin, University of Houston Law Center, Harvard, the Collective Intelligence Project, and DC Abundance has formed to build the field, with an initial research agenda followed by a call for papers and an essay series on Lawfare.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: An organized academic-legal coalition is the usual precursor to model legislation; track its published questions as a preview of future policy language.
insights.locator: RESEARCH AGENDA

insights.claim: The agenda is organized into four strands — values, process and authority, technical, and enforcement — with the enforcement strand explicitly asking how to detect and respond when models diverge from selected values.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The enforcement strand implies demand for third-party model-adherence auditing tools — an underbuilt category relative to capability evals.
insights.locator: Strand Four: Enforcement

insights.claim: Open questions the group treats as unresolved include what sanction or consequence AI developers should face if models diverge from stated values, how much value diversity should exist between models, and who verifies adherence.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Sanctions for value divergence would convert constitutions from marketing documents into enforceable commitments — a material change in lab liability profile.
insights.quote: If models diverge from those values, what sanction or consequence should AI developers face?
insights.locator: As AI spreads and becomes entrenched

insights.claim: A prior question the agenda flags as unanswered is what gives any process the right to bind a private actor and how voluntary lab commitments relate to or substitute for democratic lawmaking.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: The voluntary-versus-binding question determines whether lab self-governance survives contact with regulators or gets displaced by statute.
insights.quote: What gives any process the right to bind a private actor, and how do voluntary commitments relate to, or stand in for, democratic lawmaking?
insights.locator: A Call for a More Perfect Process
